memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But while the meat was still between their teeth and before it could be consumed, the anger of the Lord burned against the people, and he struck them with a severe plague. Therefore the place was named Kibroth Hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved other food. From Kibroth Hattaavah the people traveled to Hazeroth and stayed there. — Num 11:33-35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a sobering end to a difficult chapter. The very thing the people had demanded became the occasion of judgment. The meat was still in their mouths when the plague struck, and the place was named "the graves of craving" — Kibroth Hattaavah.

We must not soften this. It is a hard passage, and it is meant to be. The sin was not merely wanting meat; it was a deep contempt for God — despising His provision, longing for slavery, and rejecting the One who dwelt among them. Their craving had become idolatry, and idolatry always leads to death.

Under the old covenant, God's holiness was displayed in immediate and visible judgment, teaching Israel the seriousness of sin. We should let it teach us too. Sin is never as small as it feels in the moment. What begins as a grumble can grow into rebellion, and unchecked craving can consume us.

Yet here is where the gospel shines against a dark background. We deserve the graves of our own craving — but Christ took the judgment we earned. On the cross He bore the wrath our sin deserved, so that we who trust Him will not face it. The place of judgment for us became a hill called Calvary, where Jesus died in our place. What sobering news for the sinner; what glorious news for the saved.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you take the seriousness of sin as lightly as the world does?
2. What craving in your life needs to be surrendered before it consumes you?
3. How does Christ bearing God's judgment change the way you see the cross?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy Father, teach me to take sin seriously and to see my cravings for what they are. Thank You that Christ bore the judgment I deserved. Keep my heart content and faithful in You. Amen.
